<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, skip this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to EnterPlanMode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke Skill tool" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to EnterPlanMode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke Skill tool" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke Skill tool" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.


</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/357
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

`entire clean --all` previously hung silently for many seconds (or indefinitely on repos with lots of archived v2 generations) before any output appeared, and Ctrl-C wouldn't reliably escape because go-git's tree iteration ignores context cancellation.

After incorporating review feedback, this PR makes the following changes:

1. Trust `generation.json` over raw transcripts **(TRADE-OFF, please see below).** This is the primary fix; on a real repo with 18 archived generations the command now completes in ~1s instead of hanging for almost a minute.
2. **Concurrent v2 enumeration.** v2 archived-generation listing runs in a goroutine concurrent with the fast local enumeration, with a derived context so a failure in the local path cancels the v2 path immediately rather than blocking on it.
3. **Reliable Ctrl-C, scoped to this command.** Inside `runCleanAll` only, an `installForceExitOnSecondSignal` helper arms a second-Ctrl-C → `os.Exit(130)` escape hatch in case the rare slow tree-walk fallback is hit and go-git refuses to honor cancellation. `main.go`'s top-level signal handling is unchanged. A `ctx.Err()` check between candidates lets the first Ctrl-C exit cleanly between generations, and `context.Canceled` is mapped to `NewSilentError` so cancellation exits quietly without printing `Error: ...`.

## Trade-off, please read

The hot path was walking every archived checkpoint's full-tree via go-git and parsing each transcript JSONL to derive timestamps. That's where the multi-second-per-generation hang came from. Archived `/full/` refs intentionally don't carry per-session `metadata.json` (the split is: `/main` has metadata + prompts, `/full` has transcripts only), so `generation.json` at the tree root was the only cheap source — and the prior code consulted it only as a fallback when the tree walk found no timestamps.

This PR **inverts the preference**: read `generation.json` first; fall back to the tree walk only when `generation.json` is missing or incomplete. `generation.json` is written at archival time and actively maintained by `generation_repair.go`, so in practice it is authoritative.

**Behavioral implications:**

| `generation.json` state | Outcome |
|---|---|

## Summary

`entire clean --all` previously hung silently for many seconds (or indefinitely on repos with lots of archived v2 generations) before any output appeared, and Ctrl-C wouldn't reliably escape because go-git's tree iteration ignores context cancellation.

After incorporating review feedback, this PR makes the following changes:

1. Trust `generation.json` over raw transcripts **(TRADE-OFF, please see below).** This is the primary fix; on a real repo with 18 archived generations the command now completes in ~1s instead of hanging for almost a minute.
2. **Concurrent v2 enumeration.** v2 archived-generation listing runs in a goroutine concurrent with the fast local enumeration, with a derived context so a failure in the local path cancels the v2 path immediately rather than blocking on it.
3. **Reliable Ctrl-C, scoped to this command.** Inside `runCleanAll` only, an `installForceExitOnSecondSignal` helper arms a second-Ctrl-C → `os.Exit(130)` escape hatch in case the rare slow tree-walk fallback is hit and go-git refuses to honor cancellation. `main.go`'s top-level signal handling is unchanged. A `ctx.Err()` check between candidates lets the first Ctrl-C exit cleanly between generations, and `context.Canceled` is mapped to `NewSilentError` so cancellation exits quietly without printing `Error: ...`.

## Trade-off, please read

The hot path was walking every archived checkpoint's full-tree via go-git and parsing each transcript JSONL to derive timestamps. That's where the multi-second-per-generation hang came from. Archived `/full/` refs intentionally don't carry per-session `metadata.json` (the split is: `/main` has metadata + prompts, `/full` has transcripts only), so `generation.json` at the tree root was the only cheap source — and the prior code consulted it only as a fallback when the tree walk found no timestamps.

This PR **inverts the preference**: read `generation.json` first; fall back to the tree walk only when `generation.json` is missing or incomplete. `generation.json` is written at archival time and actively maintained by `generation_repair.go`, so in practice it is authoritative.

| `generation.json` state | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Matches reality (normal case) | No observable difference; cleanup is orders of magnitude faster. |

| Stale/wrong, says "older than actual" | Generation is cleaned up before its real newest timestamp passes retention. **Unsafe direction** — data deleted prematurely. Mitigation: `generation_repair.go` keeps `generation.json` correct. |

The test `TestCleanCmd_All_UsesRawTranscriptTimeForV2GenerationRetention` previously pinned the opposite preference. It's renamed to `TestCleanCmd_All_PrefersGenerationJSONOverRawTranscript`, its assertion is flipped, and the inline comment documents the new contract.

If a user reports a generation deleted prematurely due to a wrong `generation.json`, the cheapest fix is to run the repair pass; the next-cheapest is to revert the preference inversion in `cleanup.go` (~6 lines).

This PR improves the UX and runtime of `entire clean --all` by making v2 archived generation enumeration faster and visibly “in progress”, and by adding a reliable two-step SIGINT escape hatch for long-running operations that ignore context cancellation.

**Changes:**
- Adds a second-signal handler in `main.go` to force-exit (code 130) if cancellation doesn’t stop the process.
- Runs v2 archived generation enumeration concurrently with local enumeration, printing an immediate status line plus per-generation scanning progress.
- Speeds up v2 retention decisions by preferring `generation.json` timestamps and falling back to expensive tree-walk transcript timestamp derivation only when needed; updates/renames the related test accordingly.

  {
    "id": 3223067023,
    "user": "Copilot",
    "path": "cmd/entire/main.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "Because the two-signal escape hatch depends on receiving a *second* signal, using a size-1 sigChan can drop the second SIGINT if the user presses Ctrl-C twice quickly (signal.Notify drops when the channel is full). Consider increasing the buffer to 2 so the second signal is reliably observed and triggers os.Exit(130).",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 35,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "d1924fe3fddf44c0d9a24459623e5b44f41b3b5d"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223067035,
    "user": "Copilot",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/clean.go",
    "line": 313,
    "body": "On the error path from ListAllItems, this waits for the v2 enumeration goroutine to finish before returning. If v2 enumeration is slow/hung (the scenario this PR is addressing), an unrelated failure in ListAllItems can still block for a long time. Consider using a derived context for the v2 goroutine and canceling it on early errors, and/or returning without waiting (or waiting only with a select on ctx.Done()).",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 304,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "74da9d5099fd638763b379758ce59ed04deafa77"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223067050,
    "user": "Copilot",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "Returning a wrapped error on ctx cancellation will surface as a printed error and exit code 1 in main.go. If the intent is for first Ctrl-C to exit cleanly, consider returning ctx.Err() (or having the caller map context.Canceled to cli.NewSilentError(ctx.Err())) so cancellation doesn’t show up as a failure message.\n",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 373,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "54eecf0c86d9258f22818decd21ee0a11b7e4946"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223085228,
    "user": "computermode",
    "path": "cmd/entire/main.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "hmm I'm not sure we want to have this exit at the top level here - I only intend to add it for `entire clean --all` for now... not sure what potential consequences there are for allowing it at a top level like this / if it was an intentional design choice to not respect ctrl+c for other commands.",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 35,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "54eecf0c86d9258f22818decd21ee0a11b7e4946"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223102515,
    "user": "computermode",
    "path": "cmd/entire/main.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "Done — moved the second-SIGINT force-exit into a scoped helper (`installForceExitOnSecondSignal`) that only runs inside `runCleanAll`. `main.go` is back to the original single-signal cancel(); other commands are unaffected. Pushed in 74da9d509.",
    "in_reply_to_id": 3223085228,
    "original_line": 35,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "54eecf0c86d9258f22818decd21ee0a11b7e4946"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223102881,
    "user": "computermode",
    "path": "cmd/entire/main.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "Fixed in 74da9d509 — the scoped signal channel in `installForceExitOnSecondSignal` uses buffer 2 so a fast second press isn't dropped.",
    "in_reply_to_id": 3223067023,
    "original_line": 35,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "d1924fe3fddf44c0d9a24459623e5b44f41b3b5d"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223102919,
    "user": "computermode",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/clean.go",
    "line": 313,
    "body": "Fixed in 74da9d509 — `runCleanAll` now derives a context for the v2 goroutine via `context.WithCancel` and calls `cancelV2()` on the `ListAllItems` error path before waiting. The v2 goroutine's `ctx.Err()` check between iterations picks up the cancel on its next pass, so a failure in local enumeration no longer blocks on slow v2 work.",
    "in_reply_to_id": 3223067035,
    "original_line": 304,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "74da9d5099fd638763b379758ce59ed04deafa77"
  },
  {
    "id": 3223102949,
    "user": "computermode",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go",
    "line": null,
    "body": "Fixed in 74da9d509 — the loop now returns `ctx.Err()` unwrapped (with a `//nolint:wrapcheck` justification), and `runCleanAll` maps `context.Canceled` to `NewSilentError` so Ctrl-C exits quietly with no \"Error: ...\" message.",
    "in_reply_to_id": 3223067050,
    "original_line": 373,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "54eecf0c86d9258f22818decd21ee0a11b7e4946"
  },
  {
    "id": 3228231650,
    "user": "pfleidi",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/strategy/cleanup.go",
    "line": 381,
    "body": "That's a very good point! Especially given how costly the repair step during the migration is 😓 👍 ",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 381,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "74da9d5099fd638763b379758ce59ed04deafa77"
  },
  {
    "id": 3229532353,
    "user": "pfleidi",
    "path": "cmd/entire/cli/clean.go",
    "line": 343,
    "body": "Are we sure this is necessary? I'd personally prefer if one `ctrl + c` would stop the clean command as soon as possible. I think we should ensure that the context object from `main.go` is threaded through everywhere appropriately and checked like we're doing it here: https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1182/changes#diff-07318303542b6b6131c6919c8589b5880d3010571721b57d34c1b66fb081b92bR367-R369",
    "in_reply_to_id": null,
    "original_line": 343,
    "side": "RIGHT",
    "commit_id": "74da9d5099fd638763b379758ce59ed04deafa77"
  }
]

15	)
16	
17	func main() {
18		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
19		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
20	
21		// Handle interrupt signals
22		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
23		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
24		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {
25			signals = append(signals, syscall.SIGTERM)
26		}
27		signal.Notify(sigChan, signals...)
28		go func() {
29			<-sigChan
30			cancel()
31		}()
32	
33		// Create and execute root command
34		rootCmd := cli.NewRootCmd()
35	
36		// Make managed-installed plugins discoverable by the kubectl-style
37		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
38		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
39		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
40		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
41		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
42		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
43		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
44		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)
45	
46		if handled, code := cli.MaybeRunPlugin(ctx, rootCmd, os.Args[1:]); handled {
47			cancel()
48			os.Exit(code)
49		}
50		restorePATH()
51	
52		err := rootCmd.ExecuteContext(ctx)
53		if err != nil {
54			var silent *cli.SilentError
55	
56			switch {
57			case errors.As(err, &silent):
58				// Command already printed the error
59			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown command") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown flag"):
60				showSuggestion(rootCmd, err)
61			default:
62				fmt.Fprintln(rootCmd.OutOrStderr(), err)
63			}
64	
65			cancel()
66			os.Exit(1)
67		}
68		cancel() // Cleanup on successful exit
69	}
70	
71	func showSuggestion(cmd *cobra.Command, err error) {
72		// Print usage first (brew style)
73		fmt.Fprint(cmd.OutOrStderr(), cmd.UsageString())
74		fmt.Fprintf(cmd.OutOrStderr(), "\nError: Invalid usage: %v\n", err)
75	}

1	# Entire - CLI
2	
3	This repo contains the CLI for Entire.
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh
8	
9	## Key Directories
10	
11	### Commands (`cmd/`)
12	
13	- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point. Also home to kubectl-style external-command resolution (`entire <name>` → `entire-<name>` on PATH) — see [External Commands](docs/architecture/external-commands.md).
14	- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers (Cobra commands, helpers, group roots)
15	- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
16	- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
17	- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
18	- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
19	- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
20	- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
21	- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))
22	
23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of top-level
26	verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy top-level
27	shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint pointing
28	at the canonical group form.
29	
30	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `stop`, `attach`, `resume`, `current`
31	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `rewind`, `search`
32	- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
33	- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
34	  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
35	  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
36	- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `list`, `revoke`
37	- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
38	
39	Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
40	`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
41	`configure`.
42	
43	Hidden top-level shortcuts (functional, emit a one-line deprecation hint):
44	`rewind` → `checkpoint rewind`, `resume` → `session resume`, `attach` →
45	`session attach`, `explain` → `checkpoint explain`, `trace` → `doctor trace`.
46	Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
47	`checkpoint`. The `search` top-level remains hidden without a hint.
48	
49	Deprecated top-level alias (functional, prints cobra deprecation message):
50	`reset` → `clean`.
51	
52	Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `migrate`, `trail`,
53	`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`.
54	
55	The `hideAsAlias(cmd, canonical)` helper in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
56	marks a command Hidden and sets cobra's `Deprecated` field so the hint
57	renders to stderr on every invocation while the command stays functional.
58	Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
59	`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
60	named `<noun>_group.go` and `<noun>_<verb>.go` respectively.
61	
62	## Tech Stack
63	
64	- Language: Go 1.26.x
65	- Build tool: mise, go modules
66	- Linting: golangci-lint
67	
68	## Development
69	
70	### Running Tests
71	
72	```bash
73	mise run test
74	```
75	
76	### Running Integration Tests
77	
78	```bash
79	mise run test:integration
80	```
81	
82	### Running All Tests (CI)
83	
84	```bash
85	mise run test:ci
86	```
87	
88	This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
89	
90	### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)
91	
92	The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls. Named after the Vogons from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy — bureaucratic, procedural, and deterministic to a fault.
93	
94	```bash
95	mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
96	mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
97	```
98	
99	- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
100	- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
101	- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
102	- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
103	- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
104	- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.
105	
106	### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)
107	
108	**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.
109	
110	```bash
111	mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
112	mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
113	mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
114	mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only
115	mise run test:e2e --agent cursor [filter]            # Cursor only
116	mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid [filter]   # Factory AI Droid only
117	mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli [filter]       # Copilot CLI only
118	mise run test:e2e --agent pi [filter]                # Pi only
119	```
120	
121	E2E tests:
122	
123	- Use the `//go:build e2e` build tag
124	- Located in `e2e/tests/`
125	- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
126	- Test real agent interactions (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, Pi, or Vogon creating files, committing, etc.)
127	- Validate checkpoint scenarios documented in `docs/architecture/checkpoint-scenarios.md`
128	- Support multiple agents via `E2E_AGENT` env var (`claude-code`, `gemini`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `factoryai-droid`, `copilot-cli`, `pi`, `vogon`)
129	
130	**Environment variables:**
131	
132	- `E2E_AGENT` - Agent to test with (default: `claude-code`)
133	- `E2E_CLAUDE_MODEL` - Claude model to use (default: `haiku` for cost efficiency)
134	- `E2E_TIMEOUT` - Timeout per prompt (default: `2m`)
135	
136	### Test Parallelization
137	
138	**Always use `t.Parallel()` in tests.** Every top-level test function and subtest should call `t.Parallel()` unless it modifies process-global state (e.g., `os.Chdir()`).
139	
140	```go
141	func TestFeature_Foo(t *testing.T) {
142	    t.Parallel()
143	    // ...
144	}
145	
146	// Integration tests with TestEnv
147	func TestFeature_Bar(t *testing.T) {
148	    t.Parallel()
149	    env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
150	    // ...
151	}
152	```
153	
154	**Exception:** Tests that modify process-global state cannot be parallelized. This includes `os.Chdir()`/`t.Chdir()` and `os.Setenv()`/`t.Setenv()` — Go's test framework will panic if these are used after `t.Parallel()`.
155	
156	### Git in Tests
157	
158	**Tests that touch git state must use an isolated temp repo — never the real repo CWD.**
159	
160	Many handlers (lifecycle, strategy, hooks) resolve the git repo from CWD via `OpenRepository`, `GetGitCommonDir`, `DetectFileChanges`, etc. Without isolation, tests can create session state files, shadow branches, or other artifacts in the real `.git/` directory.
161	
162	Use the `testutil` helpers:
163	
164	```go

166	testutil.InitRepo(t, tmpDir)                    // git init + user config + disable GPG

name: feedback-thread-ctx-dont-add-variants
description: When adding context cancellation to a shared helper, change its signature in place rather than creating a parallel ctx variant — touching callers is fine.
metadata:

When a shared helper needs ctx cancellation support, change the existing function's signature to take ctx (as the first argument) and update all call sites. Don't introduce a parallel `XxxCtx` variant just to avoid touching unrelated callers.

**Why:** During the PR #1182 review for `entire clean --all`, I added `WalkCheckpointShardsCtx` and `ComputeGenerationTimestampsFromTreesCtx` so cleanup could get ctx-aware tree walks without touching migrate.go, doctor.go, etc. The user pushed back: "I don't think we wanted to make WalkCheckpointShardsCtx its own method — it's ok to update callers to pass context to it." Parallel `Ctx` variants are a backwards-compat shim that just splits the API surface; the codebase (per CLAUDE.md) explicitly avoids that pattern.

**How to apply:** If you find yourself reaching for a `XxxCtx` variant to keep the diff small, push ctx into the original signature instead. Touch the callers — they already have ctx in scope in almost all cases (handlers, hooks, methods on stores that take ctx elsewhere). When the user warns about scope, the right scoping is "limit which functions get ctx parameters" (e.g. don't change every helper in the package), not "add parallel ctx variants of helpers that already have many callers."
